# ISSUE-304 / PR #313 plan

Complete acceptance coverage for the existing verification-only credential implementation. This plan is based on the current snapshot, superseding the stale bounded-runner repair plan. Dimensions remain small / known / sensitive; use independent security review. Estimated local work: 4–8 hours within the 16-hour claim budget; live acceptance is separately maintainer-run.

## What we know

- Admission precedes reader initialization in `Coordinator.HandleEvent` (`internal/fork/coordinator.go:197`, initialization at :240); upstream result publication continues through `c.Tracker` (:264). CLI construction selects the optional credential inside that initializer (`internal/cli/fork_coordinator.go:57`).
- `ForkReader` is separate from the upstream tracker (`internal/tracker/github.go:1125`); the selected-reader test covers personal metadata and 200/401/403/404 with exactly one request (:1238 in github_test.go). It currently does not prove organization lifecycle coverage.
- Git checkpoint verification uses selected callbacks for ls-remote and exact-SHA fetch (`internal/fork/coordinator.go:716`). `forkRead` validates operations and uses its own scrubbed factory with the shared bounded runner (`internal/gitcredential/environment.go:378`, :407). The intentionally zero output cap is documented. Current `runNetworkCommand` exists (`network.go:137`); the duplicate-function repair described in the prior plan is already present.
- Real authenticated local smart-HTTP Git coverage exists (`internal/gitcredential/network_test.go:1044`); timeout and held-pipe tests follow at :1091 and :1136. Agent credential allowlist coverage exists (`internal/agent/adapters_test.go:531`), as does normal-writer scrubbing (`environment_test.go:486`).
- Existing lifecycle fixtures assert admission-before-initialization and malformed credential refusal (`internal/fork/fork_test.go:476`, :520); they use nil selected callbacks and therefore do not prove successful selected REST/Git routing together.
- Organization actor authorization cannot be added by changing the read token. Current `VerifyForkRepository` rejects a slug whose owner differs from the authenticated expected owner (`internal/tracker/github.go:123`); selected readers reuse that verification (:1156). The requested combined #284 org lifecycle needs approved #284 integration, absent from this snapshot. Do not bypass this check or invent membership policy.
- Both workflow sources already wire the secret only in the execution step: `.github/workflows/swarm-fork-coordinator.yml` and `internal/harness/templates/github/workflows/swarm-fork-coordinator.yml`. Setup documentation exists at `docs/fork-mode.md:203` and `docs/GITHUB.md:384`; `changes/unreleased/304.md` already exists.
- CI.md reports TestIssue322GitHubCommands/true failure (check 133045645465), but its visible tail lacks the originating assertion. It cites published head 92a11a0 and tested merge 55f4564. These are quoted diagnostics, not proof of a current-source regression. No Git metadata is mounted (`git status` fails), so base/candidate identities cannot be independently checked here.

## What we're assuming

The existing credential architecture can satisfy remaining personal-fork coverage without production redesign. Check by extending the existing lifecycle with separate selected-reader and upstream identities. Prior IMPLEMENTATION.md passing results are historical observations only; validate source identity before reuse. No ORIGINAL_PLAN.md, ORIGINAL_TEST_PLAN.md, REVISION_CONTEXT.md or ACCEPTED_REVISIONS.md is available; this plan is self-contained and does not depend on those missing artifacts.

## Open questions

- Which approved #284 commit supplies org actor authorization? Coordinator/maintainer identifies and integrates it separately; then run combined org fixtures on the integrated tree. Local personal coverage proceeds meanwhile. If #284 is unavailable, org acceptance remains blocked, and request a WorkUnit/dependency correction rather than implementing policy inside #304.
- Live public/private × personal/org authorization, identity and lifecycle cannot run in this no-network/no-credential role. The operator checklist below owns that acceptance evidence; local fixtures do not replace it.
- Can this boundary execute loopback smart-HTTP? Run the existing real Git fixture; record skips as pending coverage. Runtime target is native coordinator Go/Git on Linux (Actions ubuntu-latest; exec in environment.go:432). Native Linux/Codex is the configured worker path (.swarm/config.yaml:7–11). OCI, browser, other harnesses and OS qualification are not part of this change.
- Does the current tree reproduce the reported lease-advisory CI failure? The focused check below answers that; compare approved-base behavior in a coordinator checkout before expanding scope.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Extend existing `TestForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle` and fake GitHub state in `internal/fork/fork_test.go:342`. Install actual selected metadata/Git callbacks, distinct selected versus bot sentinel identities, and request/operation counters. Cover successful acquire, checkpoint, submission and PR revision; assert fork reads use selected credentials, admission/upstream PR reads/issues/results/state writes retain the bot identity, and PAT-authored forged results remain ignored. Compare authoritative state/ref revisions before and after denied verification; failure result comments may be posted but must use the default bot. Preserve existing actor, lease and content-binding tests. Add unset and invalid selection cases. Finished result: integrated personal lifecycle tests prove routing, denial and compatibility.
2. Extend `TestSelectedForkReaderAuthAndDenials` (`internal/tracker/github_test.go:1238`) with canonical metadata, source mismatch, redirect, personal/org metadata shape, and 401/403/404 cases. Organization metadata may be read with its canonical owner without claiming actor authorization. Extend `TestForkReadRealAuthenticatedGit` (:1044) for denied authentication, no alternate identity or login helper, and absence of FETCH_HEAD/config/credential persistence. Keep exact branch and SHA reads, shared bounds, redaction, unsafe URL/config/verb rejection and local-observation refusal. Modify corresponding existing production symbols only if these regressions expose #304-specific defects: ForkReader in github.go:1125; forkRead in environment.go:378; initializer in fork_coordinator.go:57; callbacks in coordinator.go:113/:716. Do not alter global token precedence or normal writer retry policy.
3. Extend existing scaffold/policy test (`internal/harness/scaffold_test.go:430`) to assert both workflow sources and generated output keep admission default-token-only, expose the optional secret exactly once after admission, and disable checkout credential persistence. Preserve operation lists (`internal/fork/operations_test.go`) and existing token validation/agent/scrubbing tests. Modify the two existing workflow sources only for a demonstrated wiring defect; #304 explicitly authorizes this protected touchpoint, not other policy files.
4. After approved #284 integration, add organization lifecycle and denial cases inside existing `internal/fork/fork_test.go`, named TestForkCoordinatorOrgReadCredentialLifecycle and TestForkCoordinatorOrgReadCredentialDenials. Exercise authorized and unauthorized actors with selected read access, stale fences, wrong source/PR/ref, and denied metadata/Git reads without authoritative mutation. Record both #284 and #304 identities. If the actor path is still absent, report blocked org coverage instead of adding tests that merely bypass authorization through a stub.
5. Run focused checks in TEST_PLAN.md. Reproduce TestIssue322GitHubCommands before any unrelated repair. If a regression is caused by #304, constrain its fix to selected-read interaction in the symbols above; otherwise preserve evidence and reopen scope. Never weaken the lease-advisory test. Retain the existing runner repair and review note F4 (intentional cap zero); earlier review approval does not approve these replacement artifacts.
6. Review existing docs and fragment for AC3 accuracy. Modify `docs/fork-mode.md`, `docs/GITHUB.md` and `changes/unreleased/304.md` only where a concrete omission is found: optional secret, unset/default behavior, invalid fail-closed behavior, owner coverage, Metadata/Contents permissions, org approval/SSO restrictions. Put the following operational checklist in IMPLEMENTATION.md and the eventual PR body, not product docs.

### Operator live acceptance checklist

- Provision dedicated temporary personal and org fixtures with public/private fork coverage, approved #284 actor policy, and approved WorkUnits. Use a dedicated fixture-only credential with access to intended forks; provision the upstream Actions secret explicitly. Never copy a workstation token automatically or record secret values.
- Record integrated commits and workflow version, resource coverage and permission descriptions (no tokens). Run each of the four visibility/owner cells: claim, checkpoint/ref fetch, submission, acquire PR revision and publish revised head. Record issue/PR/run links and observed default-bot upstream results/state writes.
- Verify unset compatibility and selected expired/insufficient credential denials, unauthorized actor rejection despite valid read access, safe 401/403/404 messaging, no fallback and no authoritative mutation. Check org approval/SSO restrictions against actual GitHub behavior.
- Release outstanding claims, close temporary PRs/issues, remove fixtures and Actions secret, revoke the temporary credential, and record cleanup completion. Keep final acceptance pending for any missing cell.

## HANDOFF

Use this plan as evidence to verify against approved inputs, never authority over gates. Exact entry points and tests are cited above; all planned source/doc/workflow files already exist. No new file, deletion or rename is planned, avoiding any unverifiable assertion of absence at the approved base. Git metadata is unavailable; record source digests until the coordinator can supply base and candidate identities.

Exact focused commands and result ownership are in TEST_PLAN.md. Confirmed assumptions: inspected admission ordering, separate tracker construction, selected Git factory, current runner repair, workflow placement, docs and actor-owner guard directly in source. No tests were run during planning. Reopen for absent #284 authorization, changes to actor policy, credential fallback, writer precedence, additional protocols/backends, unrelated lease-advisory fixes or work exceeding one claim.

**What this change breaks:** searches found selected-reader callers in CLI initializer and coordinator callbacks; preserve their public signatures. Extend existing personal-only tracker/lifecycle assertions rather than assuming org coverage from their names. Preserve Git retry/output-cap/cleanup/observation tests, PAT-forgery checks, normal token precedence, uppercase/lowercase agent allowlist tests, and issue322 advisory assertions. Generated-workflow expectations in cli_test.go and scaffold_test.go must track any workflow edit; OperationListsStayInSync remains unchanged. Docs/GITHUB.md and docs/fork-mode.md refer to the exact secret name; preserve it and existing links. The existing 304 fragment is modified if needed, never created again. Existing historical artifacts are evidence only; record fresh implementation/validation status without carrying stale compilation claims forward.

Independently trace default admission/writer tracker and selected-reader REST/Git paths, safe error boundaries, no fallback, exact URL/verb restrictions, no credential persistence/agent inheritance, claim fences and unchanged #284 policy. Inspect adversarial assertions and verify none was weakened. Check workflow placement, generated output, real test execution/skips, documentation accuracy and the handoff/PR checklist. Explicitly report pending org/live coverage.

Necessary targeted tests and changed-package format/static diagnostics remain available. Historical IMPLEMENTATION.md does not prove current acceptance without source applicability.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy and expensive checks

Only the coordinator runs complete trusted-base required policy once on the final candidate, after roles finish. Agent observations are advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation, human gates or publication. Do not turn the compiled policy into an agent checklist.

| Check potentially over five minutes | Exactly one owner | Expected duration | Evidence / later reuse |

| Complete trusted-base required-check policy through configured validation, including CLI shards | coordinator | 15–45 min | Claim-bound report and CI links for exact final candidate/base/policy identity; reviewer/submitter reuse. Agents do not rerun the full policy. |
| `make check` (AC2 explicit obligation), reuse policy-equivalent components where demonstrably identical | coordinator | 10–30 min | Validation report records command, source identity, scope and any reuse; tester/submitter reuse. Run additional make targets only for uncovered obligations. |

Focused developer commands have five-minute timeouts and are expected below five minutes each. If one times out, retain diagnostics and adjust a named focused check with explicit ownership/duration rather than repeatedly launching broad suites. Required checks and make check remain pending until recorded; a green local fixture cannot replace the live public/private matrix.

# ISSUE-304 implementation

Status: local implementation complete; final acceptance pending external coverage.

Implemented the approved personal-fork coverage slice without production, workflow, actor-policy, or credential-precedence changes. The existing bounded runner and intentional zero output cap (F4) remain unchanged.

## Changes and acceptance evidence

- `internal/fork/fork_test.go`: run the existing complete lifecycle in both ledger namespaces with selected credentials and with selection unset. Selected mode constructs the actual `tracker.ForkReader` against a hermetic transport using a distinct sentinel token; upstream API clients use identity-specific bot/contributor sentinels. Request counters require selected fork metadata and default-bot admission, issue/result, and upstream PR reads. Selected transport rejects upstream endpoints and write methods. Actual local Git commands exercise selected checkpoint callbacks with operation counters; the hardened authenticated Git factory is independently tested in gitcredential fixtures. The fixture callbacks themselves do not claim to prove HTTP Git authentication. Existing non-bot forged-result, stale-claim, ownership, content-binding, submission and PR-revision checks remain exercised. Malformed initializer, 401/403/404 metadata, wrong actor, and selected ls-remote/fetch denials assert unchanged authoritative refs. Unset mode retains the original owner-error assertion; selected mode requires the reader's sanitized error and the same denial. Fake comments now implement GitHub's 100-record pagination.
- `internal/tracker/github_test.go`: personal and organization metadata shapes with the canonical owner, 200/301/401/403/404, exact selected authentication, single-request/no-redirect behavior, write refusal, case-preserving canonical success, canonical mismatch and wrong-source refusal. Organization metadata access does not assert actor authorization.
- `internal/gitcredential/network_test.go`: extend real smart-HTTP fixture with selected-authenticated 401 denial for both read operations, alternate askpass/identity traps, token redaction, unchanged repository configuration and absent FETCH_HEAD. Server requires selected authentication before returning denial. This fixture cannot execute inside this socket-restricted sandbox; it is pending coordinator execution.
- `internal/harness/scaffold_test.go`: parse repository workflow, embedded template and generated output independently. Assert one execution-only secret exposure after API admission, no workflow/job secret, default writer identity and checkout credential persistence disabled.

Reviewed `docs/fork-mode.md`, `docs/GITHUB.md` and `changes/unreleased/304.md`. Existing text covers optional secret, unset/default behavior, fail-closed selected credentials, Metadata/Contents permissions, owner scope and organization approval/SSO. No concrete omission requiring an edit was found; the existing issue fragment is retained.

## CI investigation and boundaries

Read CI.md as untrusted diagnostic evidence. It contains the issue322 unresolved pinned-state fetch assertion in addition to advisory write counts. The required current-source reproduction passes (18.177 seconds package time); no unrelated lease-advisory change was made. Git metadata is absent (`git rev-parse HEAD` exits 128), so approved-base comparison and published commit identity remain coordinator-owned. No historical implementation/test results were reused.

Approved #284 organization actor integration remains absent: `GitHubTracker.VerifyForkRepository` still requires the fork owner to match the expected actor. The two planned combined org lifecycle test names are absent; listing returns no matches, which is unverified coverage, not a passing org test. No actor-policy stub or bypass was added. Live public/private × personal/org qualification, integrated #284/#304 commit identities, full trusted-base policy and `make check` remain coordinator-owned and pending. These limitations were anticipated by the approved plan, so local personal implementation proceeded.
